name: SUmiT
aliases: Study of Urgent PC vs Sham Effectiveness in Treatment of Overactive Bladder Symptoms
question: Do 12 weekly sessions of percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation improve overactive bladder symptoms more than sham stimulation?

arms.label: Percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (Urgent PC), 12 weekly 30-minute sessions

design.population: 220 adults (174 women, 46 men) at 23 US centers with overactive bladder symptoms, more than 10 voids per 24 hours and failed conservative care, off antimuscarinics for at least 2 weeks.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, sham-controlled superiority randomized trial
design.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00771264 (design, eligibility, participant flow); ICS 2011 abstract 28, Methods

verdictNote: Global-response improvement 54.5% versus 20.9% at week 13; no serious device-related adverse events reported.
takeaway: In adults with overactive bladder symptoms after failed conservative care, 12 weekly sessions of percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (Urgent PC) produced moderate or marked global improvement at 13 weeks in 54.5% versus 20.9% with sham stimulation; no serious device-related adverse events were reported.

reports.label: 13-week randomized comparison
reports.citation: Peters KM, Carrico DJ, Perez-Marrero RA, et al. "Randomized Trial of Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation Versus Sham Efficacy in the Treatment of Overactive Bladder Syndrome: Results From the SUmiT Trial." *J Urol.* 2010;183(4):1438-1443. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2009.12.036
reports.followUpLocator: abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00771264 results record (updated 2012-04-18), primary outcome time frame

results.measure: Moderately or markedly improved on the 7-level global response assessment at week 13, intention to treat; difference in proportions, PTNS minus sham (derived)
results.note: Percentages and P value from the journal abstract; responder counts and the 110-per-arm denominator from the registry results. Sample size of 214 (107 per arm) assumed 60% versus 40% responders.
results.locator: abstract; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00771264 results record (updated 2012-04-18), primary outcome

results.measure: 3-day diary after 12 sessions: frequency, nighttime voids, voids with moderate to severe urgency, urge incontinence episodes
results.note: Each parameter improved significantly more with PTNS than with sham; magnitudes are in the ICS 2011 abstract report.

delivery.note: 7 PTNS and 5 sham participants did not complete; the intention-to-treat denominator remained 110 per arm.
delivery.locator: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00771264 results record (updated 2012-04-18), participant flow

delivery.label: Eligibility
delivery.value: Adults aged 18 or older with an OAB-q short-form urgency item score of 4 or more, average frequency of 10 or more voids per 24 hours on a 3-day diary, symptoms for at least 3 months, failed conservative care and no antimuscarinic for at least 2 weeks. Excluded: neurogenic bladder, primary stress incontinence complaint, current urinary or vaginal infection, prior PTNS, InterStim or TENS use, pacemaker or implantable defibrillator; investigators could also exclude on history or examination, including bleeding disorders, anticoagulant use and peripheral neuropathy.

delivery.label: Centers and participants
delivery.value: 23 US urology and urogynecology centers; 220 participants (174 women, 46 men); mean age 62.5 years with PTNS and 60.2 years with sham.

delivery.label: PTNS technique
delivery.value: Urgent PC device; 34-gauge needle electrode inserted near the posterior tibial nerve with an active surface electrode; 30-minute weekly sessions for 12 weeks.

delivery.label: Sham technique
delivery.value: Streitberger placebo needle giving the sensation of a needle without skin penetration, TENS pads above and below the small toe giving the sensation of stimulation without tibial nerve activation, an inactive surface electrode, and reproduced device sounds.

reports.label: STEP 24-month results
reports.citation: Peters KM, Carrico DJ, MacDiarmid SA, et al. "Sustained Therapeutic Effects of Percutaneous Tibial Nerve Stimulation: 24-Month Results of the STEP Study." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2013;32(1):24-29. doi:10.1002/nau.22266
reports.followUp: 24 months after initial treatment success and a 14-week taper

results.measure: Participants remaining in the study at 24 months
Mean treatments per month among 45 participants from study months 6 to 24 after the 14-week taper
Change from pre-treatment baseline at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months
results.note: Frequency, urge incontinence episodes, nighttime voids and moderate to severe urgency episodes were significantly improved at each time point; OAB-q symptom severity and quality-of-life scores improved at each tested time point.

values.exp: 5 mild events of unknown relation to treatment

delivery.label: Maintenance protocol
delivery.value: 14-week tapering protocol after 12 weekly treatments, then a personal treatment plan set by investigator and participant.

delivery.value: Fixed 14-week tapering protocol after 12 weekly treatments, then a personal treatment plan; 50 SUmiT participants who met the primary effectiveness end point were enrolled.
